_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 72: Post-Market Monitoring
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. No standalone harmonised standard is requested specifically for Article 72. Post-market monitoring processes form part of the quality-management-system work item (Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, point 9), which resulted in EN 18286:2026; they are therefore relevant to EN 18286:2026 through Article 17(1)(h), but this does not create an independent presumption of conformity with Article 72. Article 72(3) requires Commission guidance, including a template, on the post-market monitoring plan by 2 September 2027.
basis: EU AI Act Recital 155 (legislative intent on post-market monitoring)
Decision No 768/2008/EC -- common framework for the marketing of products (New Legislative Framework)
_metadata.awaiting_standard: No standalone harmonised standard is requested specifically for Article 72. Post-market monitoring processes form part of the quality-management-system work item (Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, point 9), which resulted in EN 18286:2026; they are therefore relevant to EN 18286:2026 through Article 17(1)(h), but this does not create an independent presumption of conformity with Article 72. requirements.title: Post-Market Monitoring System
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST establish and document a post-market monitoring system that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system.
requirements.rationale: Art. 72(1) requires a documented, proportionate monitoring system.
required_content: Description of the monitoring system and its scope

requirements.title: Active Data Collection and Analysis
requirements.requirement: The post-market monitoring system MUST actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data on the performance of the high-risk AI system throughout its lifetime, which may be provided by deployers or collected through other sources, and which allow the provider to evaluate the continuous compliance of the system with the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2. Where relevant, post-market monitoring MUST include an analysis of the interaction with other AI systems. This obligation does not cover sensitive operational data of deployers which are law-enforcement authorities (Article 72(2)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 72(2) requires active, systematic, and ongoing monitoring throughout the system lifetime.
acceptable_implementations: Drift detection and model degradation monitoring
User feedback collection and analysis pipelines

requirements.title: Post-Market Monitoring Plan
requirements.requirement: The post-market monitoring system MUST be based on a post-market monitoring plan, and the plan MUST be part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV (Article 72(3)). For high-risk AI systems covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I, where a post-market monitoring system and plan are already established under that legislation, and for high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III, point 5, placed on the market or put into service by financial institutions subject to Union financial services law on internal governance, the provider MAY integrate, as appropriate, the necessary elements of Article 72(1) to (3), using the template referred to in Article 72(3), into the systems and plans already existing, provided that it achieves an equivalent level of protection (Article 72(4)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 72(3) requires a formal plan integrated into technical documentation.
required_content: Review and update schedule for the plan itself
